subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos(2 Tan⁻¹(1/7)) = sin(4 Tan⁻¹(1/3)).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.74 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 78.2. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. The twin of 78.1, with a FOUR on the right instead of a two. sin4β is handled as sin(2(2β)) — the double-angle formula applied twice, with tan2β computed in between. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Evaluate the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark. Identical left side to the sin(2 Tan⁻¹(3/4)) question, and it gives the same 24/25.
steps.memory_tip: cos 2α = (1 − tan²α)/(1 + tan²α) takes tanα directly: (1 − 1/49)/(1 + 1/49) = 24/25.

recall.must_convey: That the left side is cos2α with tanα = 1/7, giving 24/25.

the left hand side is twenty four over twenty five

steps.why: The left side, cos(2 Tan⁻¹(1/7)), is word for word the one in the sin(2 Tan⁻¹(3/4)) question, so its value is already known — only the right side is new.
common_mistakes: Recomputing it differently and getting a mismatch.

steps.label: Find tan2β first
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Compute tan2β first. Then 4β = 2(2β), and sin2θ = 2tanθ/(1 + tan²θ) is used with θ = 2β.
steps.memory_tip: Get tan 2β first, then treat 4β as 2(2β) and use sin2θ = 2tanθ/(1 + tan²θ) with θ = 2β.

recall.must_convey: That tan2β is computed first as 3/4, so that 4β can be treated as 2(2β).
accept: find tan two beta first which is three quarters then four beta is two times two beta

steps.why: sin4θ can be written in terms of tanθ, but that formula is long. Finding tan2θ first lets the short sin2θ formula be used on 2β.
common_mistakes: Trying to double the angle twice in one line.
Using the sin2θ formula where the tan2θ one is needed.

steps.label: Evaluate sin4β and compare
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Now sin4β = sin(2(2β)) uses the same tangent form, with tan2β = 3/4 — which is exactly the 3/4 in the sin(2 Tan⁻¹(3/4)) question, so the answer is the same 24/25.
steps.memory_tip: Use tan 2β = 3/4, not tanβ, in the final formula. Then state that both sides are 24/25.

lines.text: (4β = 2 × 2β, so use the sin2θ formula with θ = 2β)

recall.must_convey: That sin4β is evaluated as sin(2(2β)) using tan2β = 3/4, giving 24/25, and that both sides are then stated equal.
accept: sin four beta is sin of two times two beta which with tan two beta three quarters gives twenty four over twenty five so both sides agree

the right side matches the left

steps.why: tan2β came out as 3/4 — exactly the tangent in the sin(2 Tan⁻¹(3/4)) question. That is why both questions reach the same number, and it is not a coincidence.
common_mistakes: Using tanβ instead of tan2β in the final formula.
Never stating that the two sides agree.

insider_note: The right side is 4Tan⁻¹, so find tan2β = 3/4 first and treat sin4β as sin(2 · 2β). Using a quadruple-angle formula is far longer.
